economics.growth-diagram.0002.all: Boom (peak above trend), downturn/recession (falling), slump/trough (lowest point) - in order boom, recession, slump before recovery.

economics.growth-evaluate-1.0003.all: Plan: jobs, incomes, tax revenue vs air pollution, inequality, resource depletion, inflation; depends on sustainability/distribution; judgement not always.

economics.growth-evaluate-2.0001.all: Plan: falling AD/spending -> lower demand-pull, possible deflation; energy prices -> cost-push persists (stagflation); depends on duration, exchange rate, policy; judgement.

economics.growth-evaluate-3.0003.all: Plan: low income C€4,000 -> growth reduces poverty, funds services; but time lags, opportunity cost, conflicts (inflation, environment, inequality, BoP); judgement.

economics.growth-explain.0016.all: Population grew faster than GDP (1), so real GDP per capita fell by about 1% (1), so average living standards in Belmora likely fell (1).

economics.growth-mcq-class.0004.all: C - discovery of new natural resources

economics.inflation-analyse-1.0005.all: Plan: cost-push - energy and food prices raise firms' costs; wage-price spiral from wage demands; demand-pull if AD exceeds supply.

economics.inflation-analyse-2.0003.all: Plan: higher rate (4.5%) raises borrowing costs, encourages saving -> lower C and I -> AD falls -> lower demand-pull inflation; stronger currency cheaper imports; time lags.

economics.inflation-analyse-3.0003.all: Plan: delayed spending -> lower AD -> lower output, profits, jobs -> further price falls (deflationary spiral); real debt burden rises.

economics.inflation-assess-1.0003.all: Plan: consumers - lower real incomes, savings eroded; firms - higher costs, menu costs, uncertainty, less competitive exports; but borrowers gain, wages may rise; judgement.

economics.inflation-assess-2.0005.all: Plan: rates cut AD/demand-pull; but inflation here is cost-push (energy) so less effective, time lags, hurt growth; alternatives fiscal, supply-side; judgement.

economics.inflation-assess-3.0004.all: Plan: harmful - delayed purchases, falling AD, unemployment, real debt; but if from productivity/cheaper imports (benign) raises real incomes; depends on cause/duration.

economics.inflation-define1.0007.all: Income adjusted for inflation; the quantity of goods and services that money income can buy.

economics.inflation-define2.0006.all: Costs to firms of changing prices (1), e.g. reprinting menus/price lists (1).

economics.inflation-describe.0018.all: Rise in consumer spending (1), e.g. due to an income tax cut or lower interest rates, so AD exceeds productive capacity (1).

economics.inflation-evaluate-1.0004.all: Plan: as assess-1 with sustained judgement (depends on wage growth, duration).

economics.inflation-evaluate-2.0001.all: Plan: as assess-2 for Gallendra; judgement.

economics.inflation-evaluate-3.0004.all: Plan: as assess-3 for Sundara, 16 months suggests entrenched expectations; judgement.

economics.inflation-explain.0006.all: Prices rose faster than pay (1), so real incomes fell by about 4% (1), so workers can buy fewer goods/services (1).

economics.inflation-mcq-class.0004.all: A - a large cut in income tax

economics.inflation-state.0001.all: Menu costs / higher costs of raw materials / loss of international competitiveness

economics.inflation-state-class.0002.all: Cut in income tax / lower interest rates / rise in government spending

economics.intervention-analyse-1.0001.all: Plan: rent 24% below market -> tenants who get flats pay less, more disposable income; but supply falls (landlords sell), demand rises -> shortage, queues; poorer maintenance/quality; black market.

economics.inflation-data.0004.b: Plan: cost-push from energy/food; wage-price spiral; demand-pull.
economics.inflation-data.0004.c: Plan: consumers real income/savings vs firms costs/competitiveness; judgement.

economics.inflation-analyse-1.0005.problem: Question asks for causes of inflation, but 3 of the 5 indicative points (falling real incomes, savers lose, menu costs/uncertainty) are effects, not causes.
economics.inflation-analyse-1.0005.fix: Replace effect bullets with causes: demand-pull (AD exceeding capacity, e.g. rising spending/credit), wage-price spiral expectations, depreciation raising import prices.

economics.inflation-data.0004.problem: Part (b): Question asks for causes of inflation, but 3 of the 5 indicative points (falling real incomes, savers lose, menu costs/uncertainty) are effects, not causes.
economics.inflation-data.0004.fix: (a) 122.73 is correct. (b) Replace effect bullets with causes: demand-pull (AD exceeding capacity, e.g. rising spending/credit), wage-price spiral expectations, depreciation raising import prices.
